_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: the marginal risk difference, integrated by fixture.truth() and checked with scipy quad

agreement.claim: both engines report the same AIPW estimate, influence-function SE, and single-model comparators
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: at most 1.2e-9. harness/causal_examples.test.py breaks each working model in turn over 100 seeds: AIPW's bias stays under 0.01 while the single-model estimator's exceeds 0.08.

recovery.claim: the risk difference is close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: The committed fixture's estimate (0.103) is 0.043 from the truth, about two standard errors; inside the tolerance, and the reason the tolerance is measured rather than guessed. Measured by harness/causal_examples.test.py, running python.py on seeds 0 to 99.
